newsitem.title: GERMANY: Some Lufthansa travel agents plan protest.
newsitem.headline: Some Lufthansa travel agents plan protest.

text.p: A group of more than 150 German travel agencies plan an added "consumer booking fee" on Deutsche Lufthansa AG domestic flights to protest at its proposed cuts to their commissions, the group said on Thursday.
Bookings could also be switched to rival carriers such as Deutsche BA and Eurowings which have pledged to hold commissions at existing levels, they warned.

The warning came as the German airline said earlier around 92 percent of its 2,084 agents had signed the new agency contracts, which from July 1 will cut commission payments on sales of domestic tickets to five percent from nine percent from July 1.
But Rainer Jansen, director of the 158-outlet consortium Tour Contact, said in response to enquiries: "Five per cent is impossible for us."
Jansen said that from July 1 the entire Tour Contact group would charge clients an extra 20 marks ($11.66) for Lufthansa domestic flights but not for rival Deutsche BA or Eurowings.

Klaus Laepple, owner of Reisebuero Ko in Duesseldorf and president of the German independent agents association ASR, said his agency would also introduce a fee from July 1 and was recommending that others follow his move.
Agents are estimated to generate up to 90 percent of Lufthansa's Germany ticket sales revenue of 6.7 billion marks, including two billion marks' worth of domestic flight sales.

Leonard Reeb, director of the larger German travel agents association DRV, said many agents had been forced to sign the Lufthansa contracts because they could not survive without the national carrier.
